target_customer: Physician organizations and clinics that must report quality measures for value-based payment programs
problem: Calculating HEDIS and Medicare quality measures and MIPS reporting takes large administrative and IT effort; Able Health automated it.
business_model: B2B SaaS per clinician (later sold at about 199 USD per clinician per year under Health Catalyst)
product_category: Healthcare quality measure and MIPS reporting software

founders.name: Rachel Katz
founders.background_notes: Stayed on as SVP of Able Health product solutions at Health Catalyst after acquisition.

competitors.name: Innovaccer
competitors.what: MIPS reporting platform calculating registry measures and eCQMs

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting EHR and warehouse data and computing certified measures is data engineering heavy with domain specification risk.

defensibility.rationale: Qualified registry status and EHR integrations raised switching costs, but the measures are public specifications.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Health Catalyst bought it in February 2020 for 27M USD and rebranded the product MeasureAble.

market_need_then: MACRA and MIPS began January 1, 2017, forcing clinicians to report quality measures for payment adjustments, which created regulation driven demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and mission led (doctors paid more for quality)

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the MIPS launch but no sourced brand evidence; name resembles other Able and Ayble health companies.

outcome_analysis: Able Health rode MIPS reporting regulation that began in 2017, launched an end to end MIPS platform that January and was acquired by Health Catalyst in February 2020 for 27M USD plus a possible earnout. With only about 4M USD reported raised, the exit was modest but positive, and the product lives on as MeasureAble.
notes: No individual rounds are verified: CB Insights and Dealroom report about 4M USD total with Great Oaks, Soma Capital and Refactor, and CB Insights lists an undisclosed seed dated 2016-03-24; Dealroom's February 2020 Series A reflects the acquisition. These stay unverified so rounds is empty. Company website returned 503 so was not read. Competitor evidence is from January and February 2017 launch coverage, near the first year after batch (W16); no 2016 dated competitor analysis was found.
